request: what does a histogram of people's heights look like?

beats.intent: A histogram growing from random heights around 170 cm, bins 150 to 190
beats.narration: Measure the heights of four hundred adults and sort them into five-centimetre bins.
beats.code:
stage.title("A histogram of heights")
hist = grow_histogram(stage, lambda rng, k: rng.normal(170, 7, size=k), bins=list(range(150, 195, 5)), n=400)

beats.intent: The tallest bars around 165 to 175 lit
beats.narration: Most people are between one sixty five and one seventy five.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, VGroup(hist[3], hist[4]), color=YELLOW)
stage.caption("Most heights near the middle")

beats.intent: Fresh axes with a smooth bump over the same range
beats.narration: With more people and thinner bins the outline smooths into a bump.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(150, 190), y_range=(0, 0.07), labels=("cm", ""))
bump = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: np.exp(-((x - 170) / 7) ** 2 / 2) / (7 * np.sqrt(TAU)), color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The peak at 170 cm marked as the mean
beats.narration: Its peak is at the average height, a hundred and seventy centimetres.
beats.code:
m = mark_point(stage, ax, 170, 0.057, color=RED, label="170 cm")
mid = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(170, 0), ax.c2p(170, 0.057), color=RED, dashed=True)

beats.intent: The area under the bump between 160 and 180 shaded
beats.narration: The area between one sixty and one eighty holds most of the people.
beats.code:
shade_area(stage, ax, bump, 160, 180)
stage.caption("Most of the area lies near the middle")

request: what do 2 sin x, sin 2x and sin x + 1 look like?

beats.intent: Axes with y = sin x from 0 to 2π
beats.narration: Start with the plain sine curve.
beats.code:
stage.title("Transforming sin x")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6.3), y_range=(-2.2, 2.2))
base = plot_graph(stage, ax, np.sin, color=BLUE, label="sin x")

beats.intent: The curve 2 sin x added, twice as tall
beats.narration: Two sine x: every height doubles, so the waves are twice as tall.
beats.code: tall = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 2 * np.sin(x), color=GREEN, label="2 sin x")

beats.intent: Fresh axes with sin x and sin 2x, the second squeezed to twice as many waves
beats.narration: Sine of two x: the input runs twice as fast, so two waves fit where one did.
beats.code:
ax2 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6.3), y_range=(-2.2, 2.2))
b2 = plot_graph(stage, ax2, np.sin, color=BLUE)
fast = plot_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color=RED, label="sin 2x")

beats.intent: Fresh axes with sin x and sin x + 1, the second lifted up by 1
beats.narration: Sine x plus one: the whole wave shifts up by one.
beats.code:
ax3 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6.3), y_range=(-2.2, 2.2))
b3 = plot_graph(stage, ax3, np.sin, color=BLUE)
up = plot_graph(stage, ax3, lambda x: np.sin(x) + 1, color=YELLOW, label="sin x + 1")

beats.intent: All three rules beside the curves
beats.narration: Outside the function stretches or shifts up and down; inside, it squeezes or shifts sideways.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"a\sin x:\ \text{taller} \quad \sin bx:\ \text{faster} \quad \sin x + c:\ \text{higher}")

request: why is the area of a triangle ½ ab sin C?

beats.intent: A triangle with sides a = 5 and b = 4 meeting at angle C = 40°
beats.narration: Two sides, five and four, meet at an angle of forty degrees.
beats.code:
stage.title("Area = ½ ab sin C")
C = np.array([-2.5, -1.5, 0])
Bp = C + 5 * 0.9 * RIGHT
Ap = C + 4 * 0.9 * np.array([np.cos(np.radians(40)), np.sin(np.radians(40)), 0])
tri = Polygon(C, Bp, Ap, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
stage.play(Create(tri))
stage.add(tri)
ang = Angle(Line(C, Bp), Line(C, Ap), radius=0.6, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(ang))
stage.add(ang)
stage.label(ang, "40°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The side a = 5 along the base and b = 4 up the slope labelled
beats.narration: Call the base a, five, and the slanted side b, four.
beats.code:
base = draw_line(stage, C, Bp, color=GREEN)
side = draw_line(stage, C, Ap, color=RED)
stage.label(base, "a = 5", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)
stage.label(side, "b = 4", direction=LEFT, color=RED)

beats.intent: The height from the top corner dropped to the base, a dashed line
beats.narration: Drop a height from the top corner to the base.
beats.code:
foot = np.array([Ap[0], C[1], 0])
h = DashedLine(Ap, foot, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(h))
stage.add(h)
stage.label(h, "h", direction=RIGHT)

beats.intent: The small right triangle with h = b sin C shown
beats.narration: In the little right triangle, the height is b times sine C: four times sine forty, about two point five seven.
beats.code:
small = Polygon(C, foot, Ap, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
stage.play(FadeIn(small))
stage.add(small)
stage.caption("h = b sin C ≈ 2.57")

beats.intent: The triangle beside Area = ½ a h = ½ ab sin C ≈ 6.4
beats.narration: Half base times height is half a b sine C: about six point four.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\tfrac12 a h = \tfrac12 ab\sin C = \tfrac12 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot \sin 40^\circ \approx 6.4")

request: how do you find the equation of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 8)?

beats.intent: A grid with the points (1, 2) and (4, 8)
beats.narration: Two points: one, two and four, eight.
beats.code:
stage.title("The line through two points")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-1, 6), y_range=(-1, 10))
p1 = mark_point(stage, ax, 1, 2, color=RED, label="(1, 2)")
p2 = mark_point(stage, ax, 4, 8, color=RED, label="(4, 8)")

beats.intent: A step of 3 across and 6 up drawn between them
beats.narration: From the first to the second: three across and six up.
beats.code:
run = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(1, 2), ax.c2p(4, 2), color=GREEN)
rise = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(4, 2), ax.c2p(4, 8), color=YELLOW)
stage.label(run, "3", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)
stage.label(rise, "6", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The slope 6/3 = 2 written beside the step
beats.narration: So the slope is six over three, two.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"m = \frac{8 - 2}{4 - 1} = 2")

beats.intent: The line through both points extended to the y-axis at 0
beats.narration: Extend the line back: it passes through the origin, so the intercept is zero.
beats.code:
line = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 2 * x, x_range=(-0.5, 5), color=BLUE)
o = mark_point(stage, ax, 0, 0, color=GREEN, label="(0, 0)")

beats.intent: The line beside its equation y = 2x
beats.narration: The line is y equals two x.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"y = 2x")

request: what happens to a triangle when you translate, reflect and rotate it?

beats.intent: A grid with the triangle (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 2)
beats.narration: A small triangle on the grid.
beats.code:
stage.title("Moving a triangle")
p = draw_plane(stage)
tri = Polygon(p.c2p(1, 1), p.c2p(3, 1), p.c2p(1, 2), color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6)
stage.play(Create(tri))
stage.add(tri)

beats.intent: A copy translated 2 left and 2 down
beats.narration: Slide a copy two left and two down: a translation. Same shape, same way round.
beats.code:
t = tri.copy().set_color(GREEN)
stage.play(t.animate.shift(p.c2p(-2, -2) - p.c2p(0, 0)), run_time=1.2)
stage.add(t)

beats.intent: A copy reflected in the y-axis
beats.narration: Flip a copy over the y axis: a reflection. Now it faces the other way.
beats.code:
r = tri.copy().set_color(YELLOW)
stage.play(r.animate.flip(UP, about_point=p.c2p(0, 0)), run_time=1.2)
stage.add(r)

beats.intent: A copy rotated a half turn about the origin
beats.narration: Turn a copy half way round the origin: a rotation.
beats.code:
q = tri.copy().set_color(RED)
stage.play(Rotate(q, PI, about_point=p.c2p(0, 0)), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(q)

beats.intent: All four triangles on the grid, the same size, beside the note: lengths and angles unchanged
beats.narration: All four are the same size and shape: moves like these never change lengths or angles.
beats.code: stage.caption("Same size and shape every time")
